architectureFindings.title: The matching layer is a file-mediated artifact pipeline, not an in-process call graph
architectureFindings.observed: Across all 31 modules in pipeline/, the only intra-pipeline production import edges among the manifest's declared transformation path are: matching_harness -> matching_contract_gate; storypackage_adapter -> matching_contract_gate; storypackage_splitter -> matching_contract_gate; visualtask_matching -> {matching_contract_gate, media_candidates}; visualtask_batch_matching -> {matching_contract_gate, visualtask_matching}; storypackage_candidate_gallery -> {matching_contract_gate, visualtask_matching}; focused_candidate_diversity -> {matching_contract_gate, visualtask_matching}; focused_review_queue -> matching_contract_gate; focused_review_reconciliation -> matching_contract_gate.
architectureFindings.implication: No module composes the end-to-end run. Each stage is an independently invoked CLI that writes a JSON artifact under reports/ or grammar/, and the next stage re-reads that artifact from disk. Stage ordering is therefore a human/operational convention, not a code-enforced sequence.
architectureFindings.method: AST import-graph extraction over every file in pipeline/.

architectureFindings.title: matching_harness.build is a verifier over pre-existing artifacts, not an orchestrator
architectureFindings.observed: pipeline/matching_harness.py:325 defines build(); it reads each stage artifact from disk, recomputes sha256 against each recorded source, and emits stageResults (pipeline/matching_harness.py:535-558) with the first blocked stage. It calls no other stage's build().
architectureFindings.implication: The harness can only report on artifacts that some earlier manual invocation already produced. A stage that was never run, or run from stale inputs, surfaces as a gap row rather than being executed.

architectureFindings.title: The contract gate is cooperative, and eight runnable modules bypass it despite unknownEntrypointsAllowed=false
architectureFindings.observed: grammar/matching-entrypoint-contract.json sets unknownEntrypointsAllowed=false and declares 19 entrypoints. pipeline/matching_contract_gate.py:196 enforce_contracts(entrypoint) raises MatchingContractError on an unregistered entrypoint (line 206). Enforcement requires the module to call it voluntarily. 20 modules call enforce_contracts; 8 modules expose a runnable main()/__main__ and never call it: build_astra_review_evidence.py, entities.py, media_candidates.py, paths.py, post_render_timing.py, prior_review_reconciliation.py, visualtask_requirements.py, visualtask_split_proposals.py.
architectureFindings.implication: The entrypoint contract's closed-world claim is not enforceable against these modules. Three are materially load-bearing: visualtask_requirements.py (produces the technical-requirements grammar), prior_review_reconciliation.py (produces the baseline reconciliation report), and build_astra_review_evidence.py (produces the canonical human-evidence package consumed by this audit).
architectureFindings.method: grep for enforce_contracts across pipeline/; per-file check for main()/__main__ without a gate call; read of matching_contract_gate.py:159-219.

architectureFindings.title: Requirement derivation is an orphaned, manually triggered producer
architectureFindings.observed: pipeline/visualtask_requirements.py imports no pipeline module and is imported by no production module. Its only in-repo references are tests/test_visualtask_technical_requirements.py and REFERENCE_MANIFEST.md:81. It is not among the 19 declared entrypoints. Its main() (subcommands build/validate) writes DEFAULT_OUTPUT, and its product grammar/visual-task-technical-requirements.json (158,786 bytes) is read by pipeline/matching_harness.py, pipeline/storypackage_data_handoff.py and pipeline/ordered_visual_route_plan.py.
architectureFindings.implication: Derived requirements enter the system as static checked-in grammar data. Nothing in the gated path regenerates them or asserts their freshness against the current StoryPackage or visual tasks, so requirements can silently diverge from the story they were derived from.
architectureFindings.method: AST import graph; repo-wide grep for visualtask_requirements and for both requirements artifacts; read of visualtask_requirements.py main().

architectureFindings.title: Stage gating contains a non-general hardcoded coverage total
architectureFindings.observed: pipeline/matching_harness.py:537 gates the baseline_reconciliation stage on reconciliation.get('priorSelectionCoverage', {}).get('total') == 107, a literal integer, emitting 'prior_editor_decisions_incomplete' otherwise.
architectureFindings.implication: A stage in a layer whose mandate is story-neutral passes only when prior-selection coverage equals one specific corpus-dependent count. Any other StoryPackage corpus blocks this stage regardless of actual reconciliation completeness.
architectureFindings.note: Recorded as observation only. Jobs 1-7 forbid patching production code; no change was made.

architectureFindings.title: The two editor-designated perfect references are not structurally homogeneous
architectureFindings.observed: The Future gold reference carries top-level granularityPolicy and speakerRoutes and per-proposal presentationOperations, semanticDerivation, semanticDerived, sourceBeats, speakerDerived, taskText and advisoryJobProposalIds. The Year Seventeen gold reference carries none of these.
architectureFindings.implication: The two files designated as a single quality target were emitted by different generator schema generations. Any later job that derives target principles must say which reference a given principle comes from, and must not assume a field's absence in the Year Seventeen reference is an editorial choice.
architectureFindings.method: Key-set comparison of both gold files' top-level and per-proposal fields.

architectureFindings.title: Current Future output is a strict structural superset of its gold reference
architectureFindings.observed: Gold future-volksgeist@2 and current reports/storypackage-02-future-volksgeist-v13-task-proposals.json (future-volksgeist@5) both hold exactly 310 task proposals. Proposal fields present in gold but absent from current: none. Fields present in current but not gold: primaryPresentationOperation, routeDisposition. Top-level present in current but not gold: contractEnforcementReceipt.
architectureFindings.implication: On the Future path the gap between current output and the perfect reference is not a lost field or a lost proposal count. It scopes later jobs toward the CONTENT of beats, visual jobs, requirements and matchability rather than toward schema regression.
architectureFindings.caveat: Equal proposal counts across different package revisions (@2 vs @5) do not establish that the proposals correspond one-to-one. Correspondence is not asserted here and is left to Job 4/7.
architectureFindings.method: Field-set and count comparison; no semantic comparison performed, per Job 1 scope.

architectureFindings.title: The Year Seventeen gold reference is a byte-identical copy of a live reports artifact; the Future gold reference has no live twin
architectureFindings.observed: sha256 of reports/storypackage-02-year-seventeen-full-task-proposals.json equals sha256 of the gold copy (b03d2357...5dc3e1). No reports/ file corresponds to the Future gold reference; the live Future task-proposal artifacts are v12 and v13 at future-volksgeist@5, while the gold reference is future-volksgeist@2.
architectureFindings.implication: The gold set mixes a still-live artifact with a preserved artifact from a superseded package revision. The Future reference cannot be regenerated from the current checkout, which is consistent with the prohibition on regenerating it and makes it irreplaceable evidence.
architectureFindings.method: sha256sum of both pairs; directory listing of reports/ task-proposal artifacts.

abandonedMirrorDisambiguation.finding: The naive reading of the evidence paths is inverted. In reports/astra-matching-review-evidence-20261004.json, the 'astra-visual-selector/' path prefix denotes the ABANDONED MIRROR, and the 'matching-layer/' prefix denotes the LIVE AUTHORITATIVE repository root.
abandonedMirrorDisambiguation.proof: pipeline/build_astra_review_evidence.py:17-20 -- ROOT = repo root (whose directory name was 'matching-layer' when the package was generated); POLISH = ROOT.parent; ABANDONED = POLISH / 'astra-visual-selector'. source_candidates() (lines 82-92) globs the same patterns under both ROOT and ABANDONED.
abandonedMirrorDisambiguation.canonicalPreference: build_astra_review_evidence.py:353 sorts aliases with key (0 if ROOT in p.parents else 1, label) and takes the first, so a live-root file always wins the canonicalPath slot over an identical mirror file.
abandonedMirrorDisambiguation.dedupMechanism: Two independent layers. (1) Content-identical files across root and mirror collapse into ONE source carrying aliases -- this produces the package's sourceAliases=4. (2) Content-DIFFERENT mirror variants remain separate sources, but their records are keyed into records_by_key, so one logical decision becomes one evidenceId carrying multiple sourceRefs rather than multiple records.
abandonedMirrorDisambiguation.verdict: The abandoned mirror is correctly NOT counted as duplicate evidence, and this was verified per-record rather than assumed.

machineVersusEditorLabeling.requirement: Machine evaluations must not be labeled as editor feedback.

declaredExclusions.reason: Governance checkpoints are not editor assessment of a beat/template match.
Machine judgments remain diagnostic inputs and are not labeled as editor evidence.
Render-fidelity evidence is outside this first matching/root-cause package unless it also appears in a template capability decision.
Inventory rows without a saved editor status or note contain no review evidence.

scrutinizedCase.concern: The filename and parser name both contain 'evaluation', and excludedClasses explicitly bars model_review_and_evaluation_outputs from being labeled as editor evidence. A machine evaluation mislabeled as human here would corrupt 49 records, including the only evidence that states which template options the editor judged wrong and which unoffered options would have been better.
scrutinizedCase.assessment: The declared human authorship is corroborated. The comment bodies are first-person editorial prose with consistent human orthography and typing errors -- 'wouldve', 'seperate', 'magnatitude', 'communicationg', '3is', 'wotldve' -- and express editorial preference over options not proposed by the system ('scrolling-screen wouldve been a good option for this as well'). Machine evaluation output would not carry this signature.
scrutinizedCase.residualRisk: The source file lies in sibling repository ae-template-automation and is absent from this checkout, so its declared sha256 could not be verified. The authorship label is corroborated by content but its provenance is not independently verified here.
